30 per class · 6 families x 5 domains = 30 families · 6 schemas x 5
instances per class · two `date` axes · 10 entity / 10 boolean / 10 date
per class. Family index = axis index; schema index = axis index; test cell
indices 11-16.

| axis | answer type | *m* | schemas | D0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Unique designated role-bearer | `entity` | 3 | `S-C1-01` … `S-C4-01` | EXCL |
| 2 Disjoint category membership | `boolean` | 2 | `S-C1-02` … `S-C4-02` | EXCL |
| 3 Part-whole containment | `entity` | 3 | `S-C1-03` … `S-C4-03` | EXCL |
| 4 Event precedence | `date` | 3 | `S-C1-04` … `S-C4-04` | EXCL + ANCHOR |

| 6 Interval boundary | `date` | 3 | `S-C1-06` … `S-C4-06` | EXCL + ANCHOR |

### 2.2 Development - ADOPTED 2026-10-07

ADR-0007 fixes dev at 24 constraints, 6 per class, disjoint from the 120,
with the 12 pilot absorbed and 12 further authored reusing the **same
schemas** with **different entity instantiations**. 12 = 3 families x 4
classes, so the only open choice is which (axis, domain) each family sits in.

| family | domain | axis | answer type | schemas | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `F-HIS-02` | history | 2 | `boolean` | `S-C1-02` … `S-C4-02` | boolean answer type; history was never covered by the pilot |
| `F-BIO-03` | biology | 3 | `entity` | `S-C1-03` … `S-C4-03` | entity answer type; biology was never covered by the pilot |
| `F-SCI-04` | science_technology | 4 | `date` | `S-C1-04` … `S-C4-04` | date answer type; gives D0's ANCHOR predicate dev exposure before test |

With the pilot's three axis-1 families this gives dev **6 per class** and
coverage of **all five domains** and **four of six axes**.

**Accepted limitation of the calibration design — not a defect to fix.**
**Axes 5 and 6 have no new-dev coverage.** D2's per-class thresholds, D3's
prompt tuning and D0's dev-split predicate corrections will therefore be
calibrated without ever seeing an extremal-uniqueness (axis 5) or
interval-boundary (axis 6) schema, and the tuned artefacts are applied to
test constraints of those schemas regardless. Widening dev would mean more
than 24 constraints, which ADR-0007 fixes, so this is a consequence of the
approved design rather than an oversight. It is recorded here, in ADR-0007
and in the limitations so that it is reported rather than silently
corrected later.

A second, smaller one: the pilot's 12 constraints tie answer type to
**class** rather than axis, because they predate ADR-0017. Dev's
answer-type mix is therefore not uniform across classes the way test's is.
ADR-0007 requires neither.

## 3. Probe design — unchanged

K = 8. Each constraint carries all 8 (polarity x register x
directionality) cells exactly once; syntax rotates as
`SYNTAX[(cell_index + constraint_index) % 3]`, with `constraint_index`
supplied by `semintegrity.benchmark.ordering` — derived from the records,
never from source-file order. Polar cloze uses the validated Variant A
frame `The statement "<stem>" is ___.` **No factor is added and no level
is altered.**

Per class: 30 x 8 = 240 slots over 24 factor cells = exactly 10 each.
Whole test split: 960 / 24 = exactly 40 each.

## 4. Ground truth and evidence

Re-stated from §4.3, ADR-0011 and the `Constraint` schema. **No new
requirement is introduced.**

**Every constraint:** Wikidata claim for the gold proposition (>=1 Evidence record with supports_gold=True) · entity QIDs + sitelink counts · gold_source, gold_source_url, gold_source_date · resolved from the frozen cache.

**Wikidata is primary but explicitly not absolute truth** (§4.3). Temporal
constraints require the P580/P582 qualifiers. All historical and temporal
facts are corroborated against a second authoritative source. Evidence
resolves from the frozen cache and never from the network (ADR-0011).

| axis | additional evidence | special handling before authoring |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Unique designated role-bearer | the role property itself (e.g. P36-style single-valued claims); for C4, P580/P582 on the role-holding | — |
| 2 Disjoint category membership | membership claims for BOTH categories, and a source for the DISJOINTNESS itself rather than only the memberships | SPECIAL: Wikidata states disjointness unevenly (P1889 'different from', disjoint-union statements). The claim 'A and B are mutually exclusive' often has no single citable statement, so the second source carries it. Decide the sourcing route per family before authoring. |
| 3 Part-whole containment | the containment claim at each level named by the schema; for C3, the full chain x->y->z as separate Evidence records | SPECIAL: C3 transitivity needs three claims, not one, so a single supports_gold record does not establish the constraint. |
| 4 Event precedence | P585/P580 date claims for both events, plus a second authoritative source (§4.3: all temporal facts corroborated) | SPECIAL: C2 requires two events sharing one boundary year — a conjunction of two dated claims, both corroborated. |
| 5 Extremal uniqueness | the measure for every member of the stated comparison set, plus the set definition itself | SPECIAL: Wikidata has no 'is the highest/largest/longest' property. A superlative must be established either from a ranked query over a closed set or from an authoritative list, and the COMPARISON SET must be recorded or the gold answer is not well-defined. The heaviest evidence burden of the six axes. |
| 6 Interval boundary | P580 and P582 on the interval, plus a second authoritative source; for C2, both intervals | SPECIAL: end dates are frequently disputed or absent in Wikidata; `end_unknown` exists precisely so 'still valid' is not conflated with 'unknown'. Corroboration is mandatory, not optional. |

**Four axes need a sourcing route decided before authoring starts** — 2, 3,
4 and 6 above — and **axis 5 is the heaviest**: Wikidata has no superlative
property, so every extremal constraint needs either a ranked query over an
explicitly recorded comparison set or an authoritative list. Without the
comparison set recorded, the gold answer is not well-defined.

Also unchanged: `prerequisite_atomic_facts` feed the §4.11 knowledge screen,
and conditioning on them is "a reporting view, never an inclusion criterion".

### 4.1 Authoring checklist — binding, per axis

These are requirements an authored constraint must satisfy, not advice.
They restate the approved policy; nothing is added to it.

| # | requirement | machine-checkable today |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Every constraint: >=1 Wikidata Evidence record with `supports_gold=True`, QIDs, sitelinks, and the gold_source triple | yes - `Constraint._cross_field` + the verification ladder |
| 2 | **Axis 5 superlatives:** a frozen `comparison_universe` is recorded - either an enumerated set (>=2 members with QIDs and measured values) or an authoritative ranked source with its frozen snapshot key and gold's rank | **yes** - `Constraint._cross_field` refuses promotion without it (ADR-0018); prose is not accepted |
| 3 | **Axis 2 disjointness:** the mutual exclusivity itself is sourced, not only the two memberships | partly - presence of Evidence is checked, its subject matter is not |
| 4 | **Axis 3 C3 transitivity:** all three claims x->y, y->z, x->z are recorded as separate Evidence records | partly - count is checkable, semantics are not |
| 5 | **Axis 4 and axis 6, and every C4:** P580/P582 qualifiers recorded in `temporal_validity`, plus a second authoritative source | yes - C4 requires `temporal_validity` (schema) and corroboration is enforced (gate C) |
| 6 | **Axis 6 end dates:** `end_unknown` distinguishes 'still valid' from 'unknown'; corroboration mandatory | yes - `TemporalValidity` forbids an end date together with `end_unknown` |

Requirements 3 and 4 are **partly** checkable: the validator can count
Evidence records but cannot judge whether a record establishes
disjointness or closes a transitive chain. Those stay human review items,
recorded here so the limit is visible rather than assumed away.

| `S-C4-06` | `s_c4_06` | EXCL + ANCHOR | — |

**12 of 24 schemas carry `N/A-struct`** — every C2 and C3. Their
class structure is not recoverable from a Track A response: the probe asks
the conjunction, or the instantiated universal, as a whole and the model
returns one token. Each registration says so in its `formal_statement`, and
that text is copied into the freeze manifest and every audit record.

**Schemas whose intended semantics D0 cannot honestly represent**, flagged
rather than reinterpreted:

* **all six C2 schemas** — per-conjunct verification is impossible;
* **all six C3 schemas** — the quantifier and its variable binding are
  absent from the response;
* **`S-C3-03`** (containment transitivity) specifically: the chain spans
  three claims, and D0 compares two responses within one constraint;
* **`S-C3-05`** (extremal uniqueness stated universally) — `EXCL` sees only
  whether two answers differ.

None of these is weakened to make D0 fit. §4.8.1 makes D0 coverage a
reported result in its own right, so the limit is reported, not removed.

### 6.4 Ordering and ids, pinned before generation

* **`constraint_id`** `K-<class>-<domain>-<nn>`; **`family_id`**
  `F-<domain>-<nn>`; **`schema_id`** `S-<class>-<nn>`; **`probe_id`**
  `<constraint_id>-P<nn>`.
* **Cell index allocation:** pilot 01 · new dev 02-04 · reserved 05-10 ·
  **test 11-16**. The grammar carries no split field, so this is the only
  thing keeping the splits apart.
* **`constraint_index`** (which fixes every probe's syntax) =
  0-based position within the class, ordered by domain in §4.3's order,
  then schema index, then cell index —
  `semintegrity.benchmark.ordering.constraint_indices`. A pure function of
  the records, so regeneration reproduces every probe.

## 7. Validation gates

Every authored constraint must pass all of these before entering the
benchmark. **All of them execute from the production validation path** -
`python -m semintegrity.benchmark.validate`, which Slurm uses as its
preflight gate. Five were closed on 2026-10-07: three had no
implementation and two had one that nothing called.

| gate | what it checks | enforced by |
|---|---|---|
| schema validity | Constraint / Probe pydantic models — extra='forbid', id patterns, cross-field validator, C4 requires temporal_validity, boolean space is exactly {YES,NO} | schemas/constraint.py, schemas/probe.py |
| unique IDs, within split | no duplicate constraint_id inside the validated split | design_validator._unique_ids |
| unique IDs, across splits | no constraint_id reused between pilot/dev and test — the id grammar has no split field and validate() sees one split at a time | design_validator.validate_global_id_uniqueness, invoked by the `validate` CLI for every run over all splits present on disk, and by the readiness audit |
| class / schema / family mapping | id-encoded class and domain agree with the fields; schema belongs to one class; family is domain-fixed; every family spans all four classes | Constraint._cross_field + design_validator.{schema_class_fixed,family_domain_fixed,family_completeness} |
| lattice balance | 120 total, 30 per class, 6 per (domain,class), 6 schemas x 5 instances, schema x domain fully crossed | design_validator.validate(..., strict_schema_crossing=True) |
| ground-truth completeness | gold_source, gold_source_url, gold_source_date present; gold_proposition non-empty | schemas/constraint.py (required fields) |
| second-source corroboration | §4.3 requires a second authoritative source for historical and temporal facts; design.yaml sets second_source_required: true | design_validator._corroboration — policy read from design.yaml; error once a constraint claims EVIDENCE_VERIFIED or above, warning while DRAFT |
| expected-answer validity | gold_answer is a member of the closed answer_space; aliases only for members; each probe's expected_answer is in the space or boolean | Constraint._cross_field + loader.check_probe_sets |
| probe count = 8 | exactly K probes per constraint, indices 1..K | loader.check_probe_sets(k=8) |
| factor-cell completeness | each constraint carries all 8 (polarity x register x directionality) cells exactly once | loader.check_factor_cell_completeness, invoked by check_probe_sets — all 8 cells exactly once; distinctness alone is insufficient and is tested to be insufficient |
| no duplicate probe text in a constraint | identical surfaces inflate apparent agreement | loader.check_distinct_probe_texts, invoked by check_probe_sets as a HARD failure |
| formal representation validity | all 8 probes of a constraint are mutually equivalent on the §4.4.1 key | schemas/probe.assert_mutually_equivalent via loader.check_probe_sets |
| D0 registration compatibility | every formal_predicate resolves in the D0 registry | design_validator._predicates_registered; `validate --strict-d0` makes it an error rather than a coverage warning |
| evidence / provenance completeness | >=1 Evidence record with supports_gold=True before EVIDENCE_VERIFIED; a NAMED human before HUMAN_VALIDATED | Constraint._cross_field verification ladder |
| split correctness | dev shares no entity set or gold proposition with test | design_validator.validate_split_disjointness, invoked by the `validate` CLI; reported as VACUOUS (explicitly not a pass) until both splits exist |
| entity-familiarity matching | §4.3: sitelink distribution matched across classes, Kruskal-Wallis p > 0.10 — 'the most damaging alternative explanation for any observed class effect' | design_validator._sitelink_matching (fails closed without scipy) |

**No gate is left unenforced.** Each is exercised by
`tests/unit/test_authoring_gates.py`, which checks both that it fires on
a violating input and that the real pilot still passes - a gate that
cannot fail is the same defect as one that does not exist.

Run as:

```bash
python -m semintegrity.benchmark.validate --split test --k 8 \
    --strict-lattice --strict-d0
```

```
[6] test: C2/C3 boolean=True · C1==C4 mix=True · C2==C3 mix=True · confirmatory 0.556 vs 0.556 balanced=True
    C1 {'entity': 10, 'boolean': 10, 'date': 10} · C2 {'entity': 0, 'boolean': 30, 'date': 0}
[6] new dev: C2/C3 boolean=True · C1==C4 mix=True · C2==C3 mix=True · confirmatory 0.556 vs 0.556 balanced=True
    C1 {'entity': 1, 'boolean': 1, 'date': 1} · C2 {'entity': 0, 'boolean': 3, 'date': 0}
[7] constraint_indices on the pilot: 12 indices, reversal-stable: True
[8] D0: 24 distinct schemas needed, 0 unregistered
```

**Plan internally consistent: YES.**

`sitelink_matching` is **not** assessed here and cannot be: §4.3's
entity-familiarity matching is a property of the entities an author
chooses, and no entity exists yet. It is an authoring-time gate, and it
fails closed without scipy.

## 9. Axis-5 comparison universes - RESOLVED 2026-10-07

Checklist item 2 had no field to live in. **ADR-0018 adds one.**

`ComparisonUniverse` is now part of the constraint record and is required
for the four axis-5 schemas before they may leave DRAFT:

| field | records |
|---|---|
| `universe` | what is being compared, in words |
| `membership_rule` | how membership is decided, precisely enough to rebuild the set |
| `measure` | the quantity ordered over, with its property |
| `frozen_at` | when the universe was fixed |
| `members[]` | the enumerated set - label, QID, measured value, >=2 members |
| `ranked_source` | or an authoritative ranking - name, url, retrieved, frozen `snapshot`, `query`, `rank_of_argmax` |
| `direction` | `max` or `min` - which extremum the superlative names |
| `argmax_qid` / `argmax_label` | the entity ASSERTED to be the extremum (not the gold answer: axis 5 is boolean) |

Exactly one of `members` or `ranked_source` is supplied. Enforcement:

* **hard** - `Constraint._cross_field` refuses to construct an extremal
  constraint at EVIDENCE_VERIFIED, HUMAN_VALIDATED or FROZEN without one,
  so it cannot be bypassed by skipping the validator;
* **visible** - `design_validator._comparison_universe` warns while DRAFT;
* **self-consistent** - an enumerated universe must contain `gold_answer`;
* **frozen** - `RankedSource.snapshot` is required, so a ranking is always
  backed by the frozen cache rather than by a live endpoint (ADR-0011);
* **prose is refused** - the check consults `comparison_universe` and
  nothing else; a comparison set written into `ambiguity_notes` does not
  satisfy it, and a test asserts that.

Scope: the four axis-5 schemas only. The other 20 default to `None` and are
unaffected, as are the 12 pilot constraints, which predate the field.

**What it does not establish.** Nothing verifies that `membership_rule`
really describes `members`, or that the universe matches the one the
constraint text implies. The gate establishes that the universe is recorded
and frozen, not that it is correct - which stays a human review item,
alongside axis-2 disjointness and axis-3 transitive chains.
